narrative: Regime read: Cautiously Neutral (composite score +0.07 on a -1 to +1 scale, 51th percentile of all trading days since 1999). Finance conditions are roughly balanced (+0.01), economic data is supportive (+0.16), and market psychology leans roughly balanced (+0.02), with the economy in an Expansion phase.

Finance: the yield curve is positively sloped (+0.48pp), the S&P 500 trades at 30.1x earnings against a ~16.5x historical average, and 4 of 5 tracked sectors are positive over the past month — the classical efficient-market / factor-based baseline this dashboard's behavioral overlay adjusts. Economics: ISM PMI is at 55.6 (expansion), CPI is running 3.3% YoY against a 3.63% Fed funds rate, and unemployment sits at 4.1%. ISM PMI at 55.6 shows expansion, with neither the yield curve nor unemployment flashing late-cycle strain. (standard business-cycle framing — sentiment reads differently depending on where the cycle stands.)

Psychology isn't pulling the read away from fundamentals right now — the fundamentals-only baseline (+0.07) and the full psychology-adjusted composite (+0.07) are essentially the same. Psychology is calm enough that it's only weighted 16% of the final read (vs. a floor of 15% and a ceiling of 55% when conditions get extreme).

Volatility this low (VIX 14.2) alongside valuations well above their historical average (P/E 30.1 vs. a ~16.5 long-run mean) suggests overconfidence / illusion of control — positioning priced for calm markets to keep going, with little cushion if that assumption breaks.
